newsitem.title: COMOROS: Low turnout of voters for Comoro Islands poll.
newsitem.headline: Low turnout of voters for Comoro Islands poll.

text.p: A low turnout of voters marked elections for a new federal assembly in the Comoro islands on Sunday following a series of arson attacks and the arrest of two former prime ministers and other opposition leaders.
Opposition parties have called for a boycott of the polls.
Former prime minister Ali Mroudjae and former national education minister Abdou Souef were arrested on Sunday, opposition politicians said.

On Saturday former prime minister Mohamed Abdou Madi and the leader of the Democratic Front party, Mustapha Said Cheikh, were arrested, and the prefecture, the main administrative building in Moroni, was burned down.
There was no official comment on the arrests. Gendarmes also went to the home of former information minister Houmed Msaidie, but found he was away in France.
The election was called for a new parliament to replace the assembly dissolved by President Mohamed Taki after he took office in March.
Polling opened slowly on Sunday and at midday many polling stations reported a voter turnout of no more than five per cent.
The prefecture building, which burned down on Saturday, contained electoral material for constituencies on Grand Comore, the main island.
Last Thursday the offices of the governor of Moheli island were burned down, destroying electoral materials stored there.
No one has claimed responsibility for these and other apparent arson attacks in the last few days.

Some 76 candidates from the ruling National Rally for Development (NRD) party, Islamic hardliners of the National Front for Justice and a number of independent candidates were standing for the 43 federal assembly seats.
The constitution says a party that does not win at least two seats in each of the islands of the Comoros should be dissolved.

The opposition alliance, the Forum for National Recovery, says it wants the polls converted into elections for a constituent assembly, electoral registers revised and a new independent electoral commission put in place.
Some 313,979 people in the Comoro Islands' population of 510,000 were eligible to vote.
Since independence in 1975, the Comoros have seen up to 17 coups and coup attempts. In September last year, French forces intervened to quash a coup led by veteran French mercenary Bob Denard.
That attempt led to the removal from power of President Said Mohamed Djohar and elections that brought Taki to power.
The Comoro Islands hit the world's headlines last week following the botched hijack of an Ethiopian Airlines plane, which crashed into the Indian Ocean nearby killing 125 people.
